title: 2.4.4 Write Both: Known Count, Unknown Count
description: Write a for loop for a known-count task and a while loop for an unknown-count task. Auto-graded.
sourceRef: designed: practice writing both for and while for book 2.4.1 'Choosing a Loop'

steps.title: Known count: use for
steps.instructions: Use a for loop to print the numbers 1 through 8, one per console.log call. The count (8) is known before the loop starts, so for is the right tool.

steps.title: Unknown count: use while
steps.instructions: Declare a variable called total set to 1. Use a while loop that doubles total on every pass, stopping once total is greater than 100. Log total after the loop. You cannot know in advance how many doublings that takes: that is why this one is a while loop, not a for loop.

requirements.title: for loop present
requirements.description: A for loop counts from 1 up to 8 and logs inside its own body. Help: 2.4.2 (for vs while: Choosing a Loop)

requirements.title: while loop present
requirements.description: A while loop doubles total on every pass until it exceeds 100. Help: 2.2.13 (The while Loop)

requirements.title: console.log present
requirements.description: Code calls console.log. Help: 2.4.2 (for vs while: Choosing a Loop)
